source_text: Ὅπως δὲ μή τις εἴπη· Πάντες οὖν ἑαυτους φονεύσαντες πορεύεσθε ἤδη παρὰ τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἡμῖν πράγματα μὴ παρέχετε, ἐρῶ δι᾿ ἣν αἰτίαν τοῦτο οὐ πράττομεν καὶ δι᾿ ἣν ἐξεταζόμενοι ἀφόβως ὁμολογοῦμεν. Οὐκ εἰκῇ τὸν κόσμον πεποιηκέναι τὸν θεὸν δεδιδάγμεθα, ἀλλ᾿ ἢ διὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπειον γένος· χαίρειν τε τοῖς τὰ προσόντα αὐτῷ μιμουμένοις φροέφημεν ἀπαρέσκεσθαι δὲ τοῖς τὰ φαῦλα ἀσπαζομένοις ἢ λόγῳ ἢ ἔργῳ. Εἰ οὖν πάντες ἑαυτοὺς φονεύσομεν, τοῦ μὴ γεννηθῆναί τινα καὶ μαθητευθῆναι εἰς τὰ θεῖα διδάγματα ἢ καὶ μὴ εἶναι τὸ ἀνθρώπειον γένος, ὅσον ἐφ᾿ ἡμῖν, αἰτιοι ἐσόμεθα, ἐναντίον τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῇ καὶ αὐτοὶ ποιοῦντες, ἐὰν τοῦτο πράξωμεν. Ἐξεταζόμενοι δὲ οὐκ ἀρνοίμεθα διὰ τὸ συνεπίστασθαι ἑαυτοῖς μηδὲν φαῦλον, ἀσεβὲς δὲ ἡγούμενοι μὴ κατὰ πάντα ἀληθεύειν, ὃ καὶ φίλον τῷ θεῷ γινώσκομεν, ὑμᾶς δὲ καὶ τῆς ἀδίκου προλήψεως ἀπαλλάξαι νῦν σπεύδοντες.
thought_title: Why Christians do not kill themselves and why they confess fearlessly
orientation: Justin is addressing the Roman Senate and people, explaining Christian conduct after recounting the executions of Ptolemy, Lucius, and a third Christian.
pass_a_gloss: But so that no one may say: "All of you therefore, having killed yourselves, go now to God and do not cause us trouble," I will say for what reason we do not do this and for what reason, when examined, we confess fearlessly. Not in vain has God made the world, we have been taught, but for the human race; and we have said before that he rejoices in those who imitate the things that belong to him, but is displeased with those who embrace evil things either in word or in deed. If therefore we all kill ourselves, of the not being born of anyone and being taught in the divine teachings, or even of the human race not existing, as far as depends on us, we will be responsible, acting contrary to the will of God also ourselves, if we do this. But when examined we do not deny, because we are conscious to ourselves of nothing evil, but considering it impious not to speak the truth in all things, which we know is also dear to God, and being eager now to free you also from unjust prejudice.

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle's conditional force and the adverb's position; 'examined' matches the legal interrogation context of the preceding section.
rejected: when questioned we make our confession without fear

choices.english: the things that belong to him
choices.why: Literal rendering of the neuter plural participle with dative; preserves the idea of God's own attributes or properties.

choices.english: as far as depends on us
choices.why: Standard idiomatic rendering of the Greek phrase for human responsibility; keeps the limiting force.
rejected: as far as in us lies
so far as we are concerned
as much as is in our power

choices.term: ἀσεβὲς δὲ ἡγούμενοι μὴ κατὰ πάντα ἀληθεύειν
choices.english: but considering it impious not to speak the truth in all things
choices.why: Preserves the articular infinitive as the object of 'considering' and the strong negative 'impious' for ἀσεβές.
rejected: but deeming it ungodly not to be truthful in everything
but regarding it as irreverent not to tell the whole truth

choices.why: προλήψεως means a preconception or prejudgment; 'unjust prejudice' captures both the adjective and the noun's sense of a prior judgment.

pass_b_english: But someone may say, "All of you, then, kill yourselves and go now to God, and stop causing us trouble." I will explain why we do not do this, and why, when we are examined, we confess fearlessly.

We have been taught that God did not make the world in vain, but for the sake of the human race. We have also learned that he rejoices in those who imitate the things that belong to him, and is displeased with those who embrace what is base, whether in word or in deed.

If, then, we all kill ourselves, we will be responsible, as far as depends on us, for no one being born and taught in the divine teachings, or even for the human race ceasing to exist. And if we do this, we ourselves will be acting contrary to God's will.

And when we are examined, we do not deny, because we are conscious within ourselves of nothing base. Rather, we consider it impious not to speak the truth in all things, which we know is also pleasing to God. And we are now eager to free you from unjust prejudice.

problems.why: φροέφημεν is 'we have learned/been taught,' not 'we have said before.' Wrong verb sense.
problems.ruling: φροέφημεν = 'we have said before' (προ- + φημί), not 'we have learned'; translation is correct, claim is wrong.

problems.why: The imagined objector is clear here, but the transition back to Justin's voice in the next paragraph is abrupt.
problems.fix: Mark the objection as a quoted objection and Justin's response clearly.
